The core challenge is to create a memory system that is both persistent and reversible. We define a state transition operator that explicitly separates the current memory state from candidate updates. This separation ensures that any new information can be evaluated independently before being committed. The operator \oplus must implement a conflict resolution protocol; without it, simultaneous contradictory updates would cause the system to diverge. By tying confirmation to a Bayes factor threshold, we ensure that only high-confidence updates persist, preventing noise from corrupting long-term storage. The assumption that operational truth can be rebuilt from raw data allows us to treat the database as the ground truth, with memory serving as an optimization layer rather than a primary source.
